claim: *Intervention boundaries.* Guidance shapes reasoning input; mechanisms can constrain actions or determine whether completed work, artifacts, or runtime states are accepted. Place the mechanism at the earliest boundary where the obligation is legible and enforceable.

topology.description: Four ordered semantic-grain boundaries, not increasing enforcement strength; guidance separated from enforceable boundaries.

required_terms: Reasoning input Prompts · briefs Models · examples
Work unit Task · PR · build Deployment candidate
Artifact / runtime Types · API seams Admission · runtime policy
Enforced only through a consuming mechanism
Choose the earliest boundary where the obligation is legible and the consequence can be affected.
bw_encoding: Grayscale publication candidate. Guidance and enforcement-capable nodes use distinct gray roles inside separately labeled regions. Semantic-grain arrow does not rank enforcement strength.
redesign: Guidance and enforcement-capable nodes use distinct gray roles inside separately labeled regions. Semantic-grain arrow does not rank enforcement strength.
alt: Four boundaries are ordered by semantic grain: reasoning input, action, work unit and artifact or runtime. Reasoning input is grouped as guidance. The remaining three are grouped where enforcement can occur. Labels give mechanisms at each boundary and state that the order does not rank enforcement strength. Gray fills distinguish the source semantic roles; labels and line conventions retain their meanings.
